ERBRoles.Description: A named role that users hold. Its default CRUD and default row filter apply to every table unless an ERBRoleTablePermissions row overrides them. Each role becomes a database role and gets its own schema of permitted views.

schema.name: ERBRoleId
schema.Description: Stable key such as admin or customer. Becomes the database role name with dashes replaced by underscores.

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Human-readable name shown in the editor.

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: What this role is for and who typically holds it.

schema.name: DefaultCRUD
schema.Description: Default permissions as any subset of the letters C, R, U and D, for example R or CRUD. Applies to every table with no override.

schema.name: DefaultRowFilter
schema.Description: Default row restriction as a predicate, for example customer_email = {{email}}. Empty means every row. Overridden per table by ERBRoleTablePermissions.RowFilter.

schema.name: IsAdminEquivalent
schema.Description: True for a role that bypasses every restriction and sees every table and row.

schema.name: IsTenantExempt
schema.Description: True for a role allowed to see across tenants; tenant-scoped tables then need no row filter for it.

schema.name: SortOrder
schema.Description: Display order.

ERBUsers.Description: The people and service accounts that sign in to the application, each holding one role. Identity helpers can resolve a signed-in user to a row here by email or external id.

schema.name: ERBUserId
schema.Description: Stable key for this user, for example the lower-cased email address.

schema.name: EmailAddress
schema.Description: The email address the user signs in with. Unique.

schema.name: DisplayName
schema.Description: Name shown in the application.

schema.name: ERBRole
schema.Description: The role this user holds.

schema.name: ExternalUserId
schema.Description: The subject (sub) claim of the identity provider token, when the application resolves users by id rather than email.

schema.name: IsActive
schema.Description: False disables the account without deleting its history.

ERBRoleTablePermissions.Description: A per-table override of one role default CRUD and row filter. A table with no row here inherits the role defaults.

schema.name: ERBRoleTablePermissionId
schema.Description: Stable key in the form role.table, for example customer.Orders.

schema.name: ERBRole
schema.Description: The role this override belongs to.

schema.name: ERBTable
schema.Description: The table being overridden.

schema.name: CRUD
schema.Description: Permissions for this table as a subset of C, R, U and D. Empty means no access.

schema.name: RowFilter
schema.Description: Row restriction for this table as a predicate; may use {{variable}} placeholders. Empty falls back to the role default filter.

ERBRoleFieldPermissions.Description: A per-field override for one role, used to hide or protect individual columns such as cost, margin or personal data that the table-level grant would otherwise expose.

schema.name: ERBRoleFieldPermissionId
schema.Description: Stable key in the form role.table.field, for example customer.Orders.Margin.

schema.name: ERBRole
schema.Description: The role this override belongs to.

schema.name: ERBField
schema.Description: The field being overridden.

schema.name: CRUD
schema.Description: Permissions for this field as a subset of C, R, U and D. Omitting R removes the column from the role view; omitting U removes it from the role update grant.

ERBContextVariables.Description: The identity facts a row filter may refer to as {{name}}. Each becomes a generated helper function app.name() that reads the current transaction token or resolves from other helpers. Seeded with user_id, email and role.

schema.name: ERBContextVariableId
schema.Description: The variable name used as {{name}} in filters and as app.name() in the database, for example email.

schema.name: Datatype
schema.Description: The value type: string, integer, number or boolean. Drives the cast applied in generated SQL.

schema.name: Source
schema.Description: jwt-claim to read a claim from the transaction token, or resolver to compute the value with ResolverSql.

schema.name: ClaimPath
schema.Description: For jwt-claim: the claim to read, for example email or app_metadata.tenant.

schema.name: ResolverSql
schema.Description: For resolver: a SQL expression returning one value; may call other helpers such as app.email().

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: What this variable represents and where its value ultimately comes from.

data.Description: The email address of the signed-in user.

data.ResolverSql: select erb_role from public.vw_erb_users where lower(email_address) = lower(app.email()) limit 1
data.Description: The role of the signed-in user, looked up in ERBUsers by email.
The identity provider subject of the signed-in user.

ERBEpics.Description: The large themes user stories are grouped under. Each epic belongs to one package.

schema.name: ERBEpicId
schema.Description: Stable key such as accounts.

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Epic name shown in the report.

schema.name: ERBPackage
schema.Description: The package this epic is sold as part of.

schema.name: SortOrder
schema.Description: Display order within the package.

ERBEffortClasses.Description: Complexity bands a story is placed in. The weight multiplies acceptance criteria into units of work, so it moves the price. The most demanding band must be named G3.

schema.name: ERBEffortClassId
schema.Description: Stable key such as G1, G2 or G3.

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Band name such as Routine or Demanding.

schema.name: ComplexityWeight
schema.Description: Multiplier applied per acceptance criterion. Must be non-zero for any band a story uses.

schema.name: SortOrder
schema.Description: Display order from easiest to hardest.

ERBDeliveryDisciplines.Description: How every quoted price divides across kinds of work. The client-visible shares must sum to 100.

schema.name: ERBDeliveryDisciplineId
schema.Description: Stable key such as build or assure.

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Discipline name.

schema.name: SharePercent
schema.Description: Percentage of every price attributed to this discipline.

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: What this discipline covers.

schema.name: ClientVisible
schema.Description: False hides the discipline from the client-facing report and from the sum-to-100 check.

schema.name: SortOrder
schema.Description: Display order.

data.Title: Assurance

data.Title: Build
data.Description: Modelling and generation.

ERBBuildPhases.Description: The phases work is scheduled and priced in. Exactly one phase is the current bid.

schema.name: ERBBuildPhaseId
schema.Description: Stable key such as phase-1.

schema.name: PhaseNumber
schema.Description: Ordinal of this phase in the plan.

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Phase name shown in the report.

schema.name: QuotedPrice
schema.Description: The price quoted for this phase, in the currency of the proposal.

schema.name: DurationMonths
schema.Description: Planned duration in months.

schema.name: PhaseKind
schema.Description: fixed-price, time-and-materials or priced-option. Drives the commercial grouping.

schema.name: IsCurrentBid
schema.Description: True for the single phase this document is asking for.

ERBUserStories.Description: The atom of scope: one selectable piece of work, placed in a phase, an epic, a feature and an effort class.

schema.name: ERBUserStoryId
schema.Description: Stable key such as acc-01.

schema.name: ReqId
schema.Description: The requirement identifier shown to the client, for example ACC-01.

schema.name: StoryText
schema.Description: The story in the form: as a role I can do something so that outcome.

schema.name: ERBBuildPhase
schema.Description: The phase this story is delivered in.

schema.name: ERBEpic
schema.Description: The epic this story sits under. Read directly, not inferred through the feature.

schema.name: ERBFeature
schema.Description: The feature this story implements.

schema.name: ERBEffortClass
schema.Description: The complexity band, chosen by what the work is.

schema.name: DependsOnStory
schema.Description: A story that must exist before this one. Drives the scope cascade; must be acyclic.

schema.name: NeedsNewRulebookModelling
schema.Description: True when delivering this story requires new core modelling in the rulebook.

schema.name: SpikeCoveragePercent
schema.Description: How much of this story was prototyped before the bid, as a percentage.

schema.name: RulebookGapNote
schema.Description: The note shown when the story needs new modelling.

schema.name: Roadblock
schema.Description: When set, the story is waiting on someone outside the build.

ERBAcceptanceCriteria.Description: What is being committed to for a story, one testable statement per row. The unit of pricing and the acceptance ledger.

schema.name: ERBAcceptanceCriterionId
schema.Description: Stable key such as acc-01-a.

schema.name: ERBUserStory
schema.Description: The story this criterion belongs to.

schema.name: Criterion
schema.Description: The testable statement.

schema.name: SortOrder
schema.Description: The order criteria are read in.

schema.name: DependsOnCriterion
schema.Description: A criterion that must pass before this one is meaningful.

schema.name: IsAccepted
schema.Description: True once the client has accepted this criterion as met.

ERBProposalSections.Description: Your own prose for the Progress Report, keyed by section. A meta table that drives the document only.

schema.name: ERBProposalSectionId
schema.Description: Stable key for this block of prose.

schema.name: SectionKey
schema.Description: Which section this targets, for example what-this-is or cost-curve.

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Heading override; blank keeps the shipped heading.

schema.name: Body
schema.Description: The prose. Supports **bold**, *italic* and {placeholder} facts.

schema.name: Mode
schema.Description: replace, append or prepend; default append.

schema.name: SortOrder
schema.Description: Order within a section key.

schema.name: ClientVisible
schema.Description: False hides this row from the client-facing document.
